description: The reference declarative ruleset fixture (issue #495, decision-define-declarative-detector-ruleset-contract). Every binding surface that accepts a ruleset in its first shipping slice (the Rust core, the CLI, and the JavaScript and Python bindings) runs this fixture as part of the shared behavioral contract, not a per-binding smoke test. Every ruleset text and scanned input here is synthetic; nothing reproduces a real credential.

accepted.description: One detector per named alphabet, plus the trailing-lower-hex validator and both specificity values a ruleset may claim. Exercises the whole value grammar in one committed ruleset.
accepted.ruleset:
ruleset-revision: 1
detector: acme-alnum-token
specificity: contextual
prefix: "ACME_AN_"
alphabet: alnum
run: at-least 20
validator: none
detector: acme-alnum-dash-token
specificity: contextual
prefix: "ACME_AD_"
alphabet: alnum-dash
run: at-least 20
validator: none
detector: acme-alnum-dash-dot-token
specificity: entropy
prefix: "ACME_ADD_"
alphabet: alnum-dash-dot
run: at-least 20
validator: none
detector: acme-upper-alnum-token
specificity: contextual
prefix: "ACME_UA_"
alphabet: upper-alnum
run: exact 20
validator: none
detector: acme-digit-token
specificity: entropy
prefix: "ACME_DG_"
alphabet: digit
run: exact 16
validator: none
detector: acme-lower-hex-token
specificity: contextual
prefix: "ACME_LH_"
alphabet: lower-hex
run: exact 32
validator: none
detector: acme-base64-token
specificity: entropy
prefix: "ACME_B64_"
alphabet: base64-body
run: at-least 20
validator: none
detector: acme-checksum-token
specificity: contextual
prefix: "ACME_CK_"
alphabet: alnum
run: at-least 8
validator: trailing-lower-hex

cases.note: the final 8 bytes are not all lowercase hex, so the whole candidate is rejected

names.description: The declarative ruleset's names section (issue #484, decision-define-declarative-detector-ruleset-contract): a names-only ruleset (no detector: blocks) adding one ambiguous-bucket name, plus the built-in no-op and unrecognized-name cases. `corp_token` is not a built-in name; `api_key` and `Auth` are, so declaring them is a no-op that adds nothing.
names.ruleset:
ruleset-revision: 1
names: ambiguous
name: corp_token
name: api_key
name: Auth

cases.note: declaring the already-built-in api_key/auth names is a no-op; the built-in generic-token detector (not the names-only ruleset extension) still resolves them exactly as it does with no ruleset loaded

ordering.description: A ruleset detector claiming the identical range, specificity, and (fixed) confidence as a built-in's own candidate must still lose the tie: built-ins register before any ruleset detector (decision-define-declarative-detector-ruleset-contract, 'Ordering and the specificity cap').
ordering.ruleset:
ruleset-revision: 1
detector: acme-tok-companion
specificity: contextual
prefix: "tok_"
alphabet: alnum
run: at-least 4
validator: none
